note: The second handover, made explicit. Adam's rule, 28/07/2026: a job is Mary's while it is being priced and Jacob's the moment the quote goes out. Jacob then owns chasing, logging and the diary. This file is that boundary written down - one row per priced job, and which side of the line it is on.

rule.text: A job is Mary's while it is being priced, and Jacob's the moment the quote goes out. Jacob owns chasing, logging, deadlines for chaser calls and updates.

checklist.source: Screenshot attached to Adam's 'Sales Checklist' email to jacob@ and marketing@, 29/07/2026 09:33. Fenster's own AdminBase action list, 15 steps from receiving a tender to closing it out.
checklist.why: Adam: 'it only concerns you from point 8. The rest will be for Mary to keep on top of.' So steps 1-7 are the pricing side of the handover rule already written above, and 8-15 are the chasing side - which is this file. Rows carry the step they are on, in his numbering rather than mine, so the register and the CRM say the same word for the same thing.
asks_of_a_chase: Is this secured work for the client? If not, when do they find out - that is the next chaser date
If it is secured, when do they decide - that is the next chaser date
Has the client lost the job? If so, who won it?
Have we lost it, and why - price, lead time, missed deadline?
Is it a blow-out - works not proceeding
checklist.unconfirmed: This arrived by email, not on the hub, so it is recorded here as evidence and reflected in the fields below. It is on the hub for Adam to confirm before anything else is built on it - in particular the separate staff-facing dashboard he describes, which is a build and not a note.
checklist.standing_warning_from_adam: Some tenders sit for twelve months and are then awarded or revisited. A quote going quiet is not the same as a quote being dead, and nothing here should be closed for silence alone.

verification.timezone: Issue times are BST, as a human would see them. Mary's job files carry the same sends in UTC, so a file reading 09:49 and a row reading 10:49 are the same message - not a conflict to correct.
verification.limit: Anything issued from commercial@ without copying estimating@ would be invisible to both of us. No row here depends on that, but Filwood does.
verification.keys: Row keys are the same slugs Mary's job board emits, so a human correction made on either page sticks to the same job and neither board shows it twice. If she renames a job, its row will appear twice until the key here is updated.

retender.crm_trap: AdminBase lead 8155 carries April's lead date, April's next action and April's lead number with JULY's money on it - Estimating Log row 206, product 'UPVC', value 7,975.85. On a re-quote the CRM updates the value and leaves the dates. That is why the row read 'chase due, 98 days' on a quote sent the previous afternoon, and jacob_adminbase.py now re-dates any row whose value joins to a verified send that is newer than the row.
